stem: Johnny is a 10-year-old boy who was involved in a bicycle collision and is described as “semi-conscious” on arrival. Which one of the following can be used for the rapid neurological assessment of sick and injured children?
explanation: The Glasgow Coma Scale is used to assess level of consciousness and neurological status in injured children. AVPU is a very rapid initial responsiveness check, but the GCS is the standard rapid neurological assessment tool.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency medicine - Trauma 3 - Head injury

rationale: The question asks for a tool used for rapid neurological assessment in sick and injured children. Among the options, the Glasgow Coma Scale is the appropriate standard assessment; AVPU is a simpler consciousness screen.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. The Glasgow Coma Scale is used for rapid neurological assessment and serial monitoring in head injury.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect. This is not a neurological assessment tool for acute trauma.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect. This is not relevant to acute paediatric neurological assessment.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect. This is not a standard assessment tool for head injury.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect. AVPU is a quick alertness screen, but not the full neurological assessment tool asked for.

source.quizTitle: Practice Quiz: Emergency medicine - Trauma 3 - Head injury
source.questionTextHtml:
The paramedic crew arrive and proceed to hand Johnny over while the team commence the primary survey. They state Johnny has maintained his own airway throughout, breathing spontaneously at a rate of 18 breaths/min, oxygen saturations 99% in air. His heart rate has been stable at 90bpm, with good volume peripheral pulses and a blood pressure of 110/70. He is warm and well perfused peripherally. The crew again remark that Johnny is "semi-conscious".

Which one of the following can be used for the rapid neurological assessment of sick and injured children?
source.stimulusText:
2

Clinical scenario 1 - Johnny

Teaching/Learning points:

Rapid neurological assessment

GCS including AVPU and Modified GCS

Prevention of secondary insult

Johnny is a 10 year old boy. He is en-route to the emergency department via ambulance following a fall from his bike. Paramedics have called ahead, stating Johnny was riding downhill and hit the side of a parked car at the bottom. He was thrown over the car, landing on the street. He was not wearing a helmet and was apparently knocked unconscious.

He is described as semi-conscious, breathing at a rate of 18/min, sats 98% in air, heart rate 90pbm. He has a large swelling to the right side of his head, and no other obvious injuries. Their ETA is 15 minutes.

The following ten questions refer to Johnny’s clinical scenario.
